answer: Use a burn registry to keep each identity on its own island. First, a new agent burns 50 tokens to a burn address and publishes the receipt. Second, the network ties that receipt to one identity and refuses a second from the same burn, so one payment cannot wander into many accounts. Third, peers check the burn before granting rights, and a caught faker loses its identity for 90 days. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 burns, about $400,000 and 25 days of checks, while a real agent needs one burn and two days. Like a falcon circling one nest, the network watches one identity at a time.
